similar in appearance to ___.  Small left pleural effusion and minimal
overlying atelectasis are new.  Pacemaker leads are seen terminating in the

ABDOMEN:  9-mm enhancing focus in the left lobe of the liver, segment II
(2:21) has increased in size and conspicuity since prior contrast studies in
___ and ___.  It is unclear if this is secondary to differences
in technique/contrast timing or represent real growth.  The portal veins are
patent.  A large gallstone is seen in the body of the gallbladder which is not
distended.  The pancreas is atrophic.  The spleen and the adrenal glands are
normal.  1-cm left upper pole renal hypodensity is unchanged. 

A trace amount of ascites is seen around the inferior edge of the liver, left
upper paracolic gutter, and in the pelvis posterior to the rectum.  Density of
approximately 30 Hounsfield units suggests minimal complexity.  The stomach,
small and large bowel have normal caliber and appearance.  Prominant duodenal
diverticulum arises from the ___ portion of the duodenum.

PELVIS:  The remainder of the bowel is of normal caliber.  Large parastomal
hernia containing bowel loops has a 3.5-cm neck.  The bowel loops are not
dilated.  Status post abdominoperineal resection.  A Foley catheter is seen
within the bladder which is compressed around the balloon.  Diffuse
subcutaneous anasarca is seen.

BONE WINDOWS:  Previously described left-sided rib fractures and possible
right-sided rib fractures are above the field of view on this study.  No
concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions are seen.  Mild multilevel degenerative
disease is seen in the lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Ascites is new since most recent exams dating back to ___, likely
correlating with diffuse anasarca.

2.  Slight increase in size of 9-mm enhancing left liver lobe lesion which is
incompletely characterized on this exam.  This might be a flash filling
hemangioma or focal nodular hyperplasia.  No other acute intra-abdominal
process.  If more definitive characterization is desired, multiphasic CT of
the liver could be considered.

FINDINGS: 

VASCULAR:

Large right retroperitoneal hematoma (9.3 x 24 cm) secondary to a right common
femoral artery pseudoaneurysm.  The pseudoaneurysm neck measures 0.2 cm.  The 
pseudoaneurysm sac measures 1.4 x 2.2 cm.  Another area of lobular contrast
extravasation/pseudoaneurysm sac in the retroperitoneal spaces superior to the
previously mentioned pseudoaneurysm measures 0.8 x 3 cm.  This likely
represent another component of the CFA pseudoaneurysm versus a separate one.

Thinning and irregularity of the origin of the right inferior epigastric
artery.

Patent aorta and major branches.  Mild arteriosclerosis.  Left superficial
femoral arterial catheter.

 LOWER CHEST: Tunneled dialysis catheter tip in the right atrium.  Coronary
calcifications.  Bibasilar atelectasis.  Moderate right pleural effusion. 
Mild gynecomastia.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: Nodular shrunken liver consistent with known cirrhosis.  No
focal mass.  Cholelithiasis.  No ductal dilation.  Moderate ascites.

PANCREAS:  No discrete lesion or ductal dilation.

SPLEEN: 14.6 cm splenomegaly.

ADRENALS: Unremarkable.

URINARY:  Contrast enhancing bilateral kidneys in the noncontrast phase,
likely from recent cath lab procedure.  The mild anterior displacement of the
right kidney from the right retroperitoneal hematoma.  No nephrolithiasis or
hydronephrosis.  No hydroureter.  No discrete mass.

GASTROINTESTINAL: No intestinal obstruction. Normal caliber small and large
intestine.

PELVIS: Rectal tube in situ.  Prostate calcifications.  Unremarkable seminal
vesicles.  Decompressed bladder with Foley catheter.

LYMPH NODES: No adenopathy.

VASCULAR: Patent aorta and major branches. Mild arteriosclerosis.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: Indirect inguinal hernia on left containing fluid. 
Soft tissue edema/ bruising in the right groin.  No acute fracture.

IMPRESSION:


1. 24 cm right retroperitoneal hematoma secondary to a right common femoral
artery pseudoaneurysm measuring 2.2 cm with a neck of 0.2 cm and another
component of the pseudoaneurysm just superiorly measuring 3 cm.
2. Cirrhosis, ascites and splenomegaly.
3. Cholelithiasis.
4. Moderate right pleural effusion and bibasilar atelectasis.

NOTIFICATION:  The patient was transferred directly to interventional
Radiology for pseudoaneurysm embolization.

INDICATION:  ___ with s/p CVA, p/w acute respiratory distress, dysphagia,
significant upper airiway secretions; intubated for respiratory distress,
hypoxia;  // eval for mechanical obstruction, pna, upper airway inflammation

TECHNIQUE:  Axial multidetector CT images were obtained through the thorax
after the uneventful administration of intravenous contrast.  Reformatted
coronal, sagittal, thin slice axial images, and oblique maximal intensity
projection images were submitted to PACS and reviewed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 284 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT torso ___

FINDINGS: 

HEART AND VASCULATURE: Pulmonary vasculature is well opacified to the
subsegmental level without filling defect to indicate a pulmonary embolus. The
thoracic aorta is normal in caliber without evidence of dissection or
intramural hematoma.  Moderate atherosclerotic calcifications seen throughout
the thoracic aorta.  The heart, pericardium, and great vessels are within
normal limits. No pericardial effusion is seen.

AXILLA, HILA, AND MEDIASTINUM: No axillary, mediastinal, or hilar
lymphadenopathy is seen.  No mediastinal mass.  The esophagus is significantly
patulous and filled with solid and liquid material, more solid at the inferior
esophagus just superior to the GE junction.

PLEURAL SPACES:  There are likely trace pleural effusions bilaterally.  No
pneumothorax.


LUNGS/AIRWAYS:  The endotracheal tube tip is approximately 2.7 cm above the
carina.  There are secretions along the superior portion of the ET tube. 
There are diffuse hazy nodular with some ground-glass opacities in the upper
lobes bilaterally.  There are dense consolidative opacities in the lower lobes
bilaterally.  The airways are patent to the level of the segmental bronchi
bilaterally.

BASE OF NECK: Visualized portions of the base of the neck demonstrate
heterogeneous appearance of the thyroid

ABDOMEN:  There is a moderate hiatal hernia.  The remainder of the imaged
upper abdomen is unremarkable besides tiny hypodensity at the upper pole the
right kidney which is too small to characterize but likely a cyst.

BONES: No suspicious osseous abnormality is seen.? There is no acute fracture.
Scoliosis is similar to prior.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic abnormality.
2. Significantly patulous esophagus is distended with liquid and solid
material, with more solid components just proximal to the GE junction,
suggesting a component of mechanical and/or functional partial obstruction.
3. Dense consolidations in the lower lobes bilaterally likely represent a
combination of atelectasis, aspiration, and infection.  Diffuse hazy nodular
opacities in the upper lobes bilaterally are likely due to infection and/or
inflammation.
4. There are secretions along the superior portion of the ET tube.

NOTIFICATION:   The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with ___
___ on the telephone on ___ at 1:42 ___, 5 minutes after discovery of

HISTORY:  Hypoxia, hypotension and prior pulmonary embolus.  Evaluate for the
presence of a pulmonary embolism.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the chest after the
uneventful administration of intravenous contrast during the pulmonary
arterial phase of enhancement.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
provided and reviewed.  Maximum intensity projection images were created and
reviewed as well.

DLP:  710.02 mGy per cm.

COMPARISON:  Same day chest xray.

FINDINGS: An endotracheal tube is 3.4 cm from the carina.  There is near
complete collapse of the right lung with secretions/mucus seen in the right
mainstem bronchus (2:43).  A small portion of the right upper lobe remains
aerated.  There is a small amount of atelectasis within the left lower lobe. 
No pleural effusion, pneumothorax or focal consolidation worrisome for
pneumonia.

The pulmonary artery is enlarged, measuring 4.8 cm in cross-section.  Contrast
opacifies the segmental and subsegmental vessels of the pulmonary arterial
tree, without filling defects to indicate an underlying pulmonary embolus. 
The heart is normal in size and there is no pericardial effusion.  Given the
substantial volume loss, the mediastinum has shifted towards the right
hemithorax.

The included thyroid is normal.  There is no axillary lymphadenopathy. 
Scattered mediastinal lymph nodes range up to 11 mm (2:57).

Limited views of the unenhanced liver, spleen and colon are unremarkable.  An
enteric tube is partially imaged but courses into the stomach.

There are no concerning osseous lesions.  Chronic appearing bilateral rib
fractures are noted and not significantly displaced.  Similarly, a chronic
appearing mid-sternal fracture is noted.  

IMPRESSION:
1.  Near complete collapse of the right lung secondary to secretions/mucus
within the right mainstem bronchus.  The substantial volume loss has resulted
in shift of the mediastinum to the right.  Bronchoscopy recommended.
2.  No pulmonary embolus.  
3.  Enlargement of the main pulmonary artery is compatible with underlying
pulmonary hypertension.  
4.  Mediastinal lymphadenopathy of indeterminate etiology.

 Total DLP (Body) = 616 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: At the partially imaged at the lung bases are diffuse, multifocal
bilateral ground-glass and consolidative opacities concerning for multifocal
infection, better evaluated on earlier CT chest ___.  There is a
trace left layering nonhemorrhagic pleural effusion.  There is no pericardial
effusion.  There is no hiatus hernia.

CT ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: Diffuse periportal hypoattenuation likely reflects edema, which
can be seen in the setting of volume resuscitation.  Tiny hyperdense foci
layering dependently in the gallbladder lumen likely reflect small gallstones
(601 B, 32).  The liver enhances homogeneously without evidence of concerning
focal lesion. There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation. The portal
vein is patent.  The gallbladder is otherwise unremarkable.

PANCREAS: Calcifications seen near the pancreatic head.  Otherwise, the
pancreas enhances homogeneously. There is no peripancreatic stranding or
ductal dilation.

SPLEEN: The spleen is at the upper limits of normal with 12.5 cm.).  There are
no focal splenic lesions.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are normal.

URINARY: Several circumscribed hypodensities in the bilateral renal cortices
measuring up to 2.3 cm in the right lower pole are compatible with simple
renal cysts.  Smaller hypodensities elsewhere in the renal cortices are too
small to characterize accurately by CT.  Otherwise, the kidneys enhance
normally and symmetrically.  There is no hydronephrosis.  Mild bilateral
perinephric stranding is symmetric and unchanged from prior exam, nonspecific
but commonly seen in elderly patients.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach and duodenum are unremarkable.  Non-dilated
small bowel loops are normal in course and caliber without evidence of wall
thickening or obstruction.  The colon is filled with stool but is otherwise
unremarkable.  The appendix is not directly visualized, however there are no
secondary signs of appendicitis.

VASCULAR AND LYMPH NODES: The abdominal aorta is moderately tortuous without
evidence of aneurysm or dilation.  There is mild calcification.  Major
proximal tributaries are patent.

Mildly prominent retroperitoneal lymph nodes have a similar appearance to
prior CT from ___ (for example see series 2, image 43).  While these
are not individually pathologic enlarged, appear increased in number and
prominent, possibly reactive.  There is no mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS:
The bladder is underdistended, with a Foley catheter balloon in situ. 
Excreted contrast fills the bladder lumen.  There is no pelvic sidewall, iliac
chain, or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free pelvic fluid.

MUSCULOSKELETAL: Along the right flank/buttock, at the level the right greater
trochanter, there is a 2.2 x 1.9 x 4.3 cm soft tissue density focus which may
represent a hematoma (2, 87 and 602 B, 14).  Otherwise, there is no concerning
focal subcutaneous or musculoskeletal soft tissue abnormality.  Chronic
superior endplate fractures of L2 and L3 are unchanged from prior exam from
___.  Mild height loss of the T12 vertebral body at the superior
endplate is also unchanged.  No concerning focal lytic or sclerotic osseous
lesions are seen.  There is diffuse subjective osseous demineralization.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of pneumoperitoneum.
2. Cholelithiasis.  Normal gallbladder.
3. Trace left layering nonhemorrhagic pleural effusion.
4. Multifocal bilateral ground-glass and consolidative opacities concerning
for multifocal infection better evaluated on earlier CT chest from ___.
5. 2.2 x 1.9 x 4.3 cm soft tissue density focus which may represent a hematoma
along the right buttock/flank.  Correlate with physical exam.
6. Chronic superior endplate fractures of L2 and L3, as well as more mild
height loss of T12.

4. Right hepatic arteriogram.
5. Right hepatic arterial embolization with 5 x 15 Helix coil.
6. Post-embolization common hepatic arteriogram.

hepatic artery.
9. Right common femoral arteriogram.
PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient's wife. The
patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol. The
right groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Under palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery was
accessed using a micropuncture set at the level of the mid-femoral head. A
0.018 wire was passed easily into the vessel lumen. A small skin incision was
made over the needle. Then the inner dilator and wire were removed and a
___ wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The micropuncture
sheath was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a continuous
heparinized saline side arm flush.

A C2 Cobra Glide catheter was advanced over the wire and used to cannulate the
celiac axis and then advanced over a glidewire into the common hepatic artery.
A common hepatic arteriogram was obtained with findings as detailed below. 100
ug of nitroglycerin was administered intraarterially into the common hepatic
artery and a post-therapeutic common hepatic arteriogram demonstrated a normal
caliber left hepatic artery without residual vasospasm.

Attention was then turned to the area of concern in the right hepatic artery.
A STC microcatheter preloaded with a double-angled glidewire was advanced into
the proximal right hepatic artery. A right hepatic arteriogram was performed
with findings as detailed below. Decision was made to coil the pseudoaneurysm
arising from the proximal right hepatic artery.

Multiple attempts were made to coil the pseudoaneurysm with a 7 x 30 Helix
coil, however the coil continued to buckle into the left hepatic artery and
was unable to be satisfactorily placed. A 5 x 15 Helix was then successfully
placed into the pseudoaneurysm. A post-embolization common hepatic arteriogram
was then obtained with findings as detailed below.

Given satisfactory post-embolization results of the right hepatic artery,
attention was then turned to the left hepatic artery. 100 ug of nitroglycerin
was administered intraarterially into the distal common hepatic artery via the
microcatheter. A post-therapeutic common hepatic angiogram at this time
demonstrated reduced vasospasm of the left hepatic artery with filling of
distal branches but a filling defect within the proximal left hepatic artery.
500 ___ was administered intraarterially into the distal CHA. A
post-therapeutic common hepatic angiogram demonstrated persistent but smaller
filling defect in the proximal LHA. Two 1 mg doses of tPA were then
administered intraarterially into the distal CHA sequentially with an
intervening post-therapeutic common hepatic angiogram demonstrating decreasing
size of the filling defect in the proximal LHA but a new small filling defect
in a distal branch of the LHA.

A rotational cone beam CT and rotational angiogram of the common hepatic
artery were performed at this point to better evaluate the anatomy and assess
the relationship of the clot with the pseudoaneurysm coil, with findings as
detailed below. Multiplanar CT images were reconstructed and 3D
volume-rendered images of the arterial anatomy required post-processing on an

used in the interpretation and reporting of this procedure.

A third dose of 1 mg tPA was then administered intraarterially into the distal
CHA and a post-therapeutic common hepatic angiogram demonstrated near complete
resolution of the filling defect in the proximal LHA and normal enhancement of
distal LHA branches with no evidence of flow limitation.

All catheters and wires were withdrawn. A common femoral arteriogram was
performed prior to use of a closure device demonstrating normal bifurcation of
the common femoral artery. An Angio-Seal device was deployed at the
arteriotomy site. Manual pressure was held for 5 minutes. A dry sterile
dressing was applied. The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no
immediate postprocedural complications.

2. Post-nitroglycerin common hepatic arteriogram demonstrating patent left
hepatic artery without previously seen wall irregularity.

3. Right hepatic arteriogram demonstrating outpouching arising from the
proximal right hepatic artery, consistent with a pseudoaneurysm, and a small
amount of active extravasation of contrast.

4. Successful deployment of 5 x 15 Helix coil in right hepatic artery
pseudoaneurysm.

5. Post-embolization common hepatic arteriogram demonstrating no enhancement
of coiled pseudoaneurysm and no active extravasation. The left hepatic artery
was noted to not enhance.

6. Multiple post-therapeutic and one rotational cone beam CT of the common
hepatic artery after intra-arterial administration of nitroglycerin, heparin,
and tPA with near complete resolution of vasospasm and filling defect of the
proximal left hepatic artery. No evidence of flow limitation. A tiny resudual
thrombus or small intimal tear cannot be entirely excluded. Further
intervention was not felt to be wise.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Successful coiling of a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proximal right
hepatic artery adjacent to the proximal edge of a right hepatic artery stent.

2. Vasospasm and thrombosis of the proximal left hepatic artery, which was
likely predisposed to spasm from prior pancreatic leak and inflammation.
Near-complete resolution of spasm and thrombosis after intra-arterial
administration of total of 200 microgram nitroglycerin, 500 units heparin, and
3 mg tPA. No evidence of flow-limitation at completion of the procedure.

punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.

dressing applied.

thrombolysis

was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle.  Images of
ultrasound access were stored on PACS. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed

at the needle entry site. The needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.

advanced over the wire into the inferior vena cava.  Using an MPA catheter and

vein.  The angled sheath was turned anteriorly.  The needle was then advanced
through liver parenchyma and the needle was withdrawn over its blue sheath.

complications.

via the needle and attempted to advance centrally, unsuccessfully.  The

fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance centrally into portal venous confluence
and into the SMV.  Position of wire was checked fluoroscopically in multiple
projections.  The headliner wire was pulled back to the confluence and
advanced into the splenic Vein which confirmed portal venous access. 
Subsequently, the needle was removed over the wire and exchanged for the metal
cannula and inner dilator of an Accustick set which was advanced centrally. 
The inner dilator was advanced just proximal to the portal confluence over the
headliner wire.  The metal cannula was removed and the headliner wire was
exchanged for a Nitinol wire which was then advanced into the splenic vein.

reformed outside the patient and advanced over the Nitinol wire centrally with
the sheath of the Accustick set delivered into the ___.  The Nitinol wire was
removed.  A small contrast injection confirmed thrombus within the main portal
vein and stasis of flow.

into the sheath and used to select the SMV and advanced distally into an ___
branch.  The glidewire was then removed and a contrast injection into the

then exchanged for a 5 cm infusion length lysis ___ catheter
over-the-wire and the wire was removed.  Small contrast injections
demonstrated appropriate positioned of lysis catheter in clot burden.  Once
appropriate positioning was confirmed, the lysis catheter and sheath were
secured to each other and these were secured to the patient's skin with 0 silk
sutures.  Lysis infusion with tPA was then administered.

extubated and transferred to the ICU for monitoring.

an Angio-Seal closure device was deployed. Additional manual pressure was held
until hemostasis was achieved. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient
tolerated the procedure well.
